text:
For most households, I’d get the **BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 + 200 W solar panel kit**. It has a 2,073.6 Wh battery and can accept up to 1,000 W of solar input if you add panels later. The comparison says it can cover a fridge and CPAP for roughly a day and night from a full charge. It’s listed at **$1,199**; [buy the kit](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2-200w-solar-kit). ([Dealectric’s hurricane kit comparison](https://dealectric.com/best-solar-generator-kit-for-hurricane-season))

If that’s more capacity than you need, the **BLUETTI AC180 + 200 W panel** is a lower-cost option, listed at **$729**: [buy the kit](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180-200w-solar-kit). ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/best-solar-generator-kit-for-hurricane-season))

One caveat: a solar kit is backup for selected essentials, not a guarantee of whole-home power—especially if storm clouds limit recharging. Check the wattage of what you need to run, and plan to conserve power between sunny periods. For major loads or long outages, a battery station may need to be part of a broader backup plan. ([We Are Salt](https://www.wearesalt.org/best-solar-generators-for-hurricane-season/))
